tokens.text_core: HIV continues to generate new diagnoses and new deaths at a scale that warrants sustained public attention. The epidemic has not ended — public awareness of it has.

text_by_persona.TSP: HIV continues generating new diagnoses and new deaths at a scale that demands sustained public attention. The epidemic hasn't ended. Public awareness of it has — and communities across this country are absorbing a growing burden that federal data makes impossible to ignore.
text_by_persona.CEC: HIV keeps generating new diagnoses and deaths at a scale the market hasn't solved and policy hasn't prioritized. The epidemic hasn't ended. Awareness of it has — and the human and economic costs keep accumulating in communities across the country.
text_by_persona.TC: HIV continues generating new diagnoses and new deaths at a scale that demands responsible public attention. The epidemic hasn't ended. Public awareness of it has — and communities across this country are carrying a burden that sound public health policy has the tools to reduce.
text_by_persona.WE: HIV is still generating new diagnoses and new deaths across this country — in communities that assumed it wasn't their problem. Strong communities don't get that way by ignoring threats. They get that way by facing them.
text_by_persona.PP: HIV keeps generating new diagnoses and new deaths at a scale that working communities across this country can least afford to ignore. The epidemic hasn't ended. Public awareness of it has — and the costs keep landing on the people with the least cushion to absorb them.
text_by_persona.HF: HIV keeps generating new diagnoses and new deaths — not because the science failed, but because the system delivering it is running on infrastructure built for a different era. The innovation exists to end this. The bottleneck is everything built around it.
text_by_persona.PFF: HIV keeps generating new diagnoses and new deaths — not because the science failed, but because the institutions responsible for delivering it have. The epidemic hasn't ended. Pretending otherwise is exactly the kind of establishment narrative that gets people killed.
text_by_persona.HHN: HIV keeps generating new diagnoses and new deaths in communities across this country — communities trying to stay whole and healthy. The epidemic hasn't ended. The burden it places on families and neighbors who are doing everything right is real and ongoing.
text_by_persona.MFL: HIV keeps generating new diagnoses and new deaths across this country. The epidemic hasn't ended. And the people who want to take responsibility for their own health and protect themselves are still being blocked from the tools that would let them do it.
text_by_persona.VS: HIV keeps generating new diagnoses and new deaths across this country. The epidemic hasn't ended. Whatever you think about how it's been handled, the people bearing the cost of that unfinished fight are real — and the burden on their communities is real.
text_by_persona.UCP: HIV keeps generating new diagnoses and new deaths at a scale that demands moral clarity. The epidemic hasn't ended. Public awareness of it has — and the people left carrying its weight have been told, in policy and in practice, that their suffering is acceptable.
text_by_persona.FJP: HIV is still taking lives in our communities — quietly, steadily, in families and congregations that have stopped talking about it. The epidemic hasn't ended. The silence around it has made it invisible. Invisible suffering is still suffering.
text_by_persona.HCP: HIV keeps generating new diagnoses and new deaths at a scale that working communities across this country are still absorbing. The epidemic hasn't ended. The costs of leaving it unaddressed don't disappear — they get distributed to the people and programs that can least afford to carry them.
text_by_persona.HAD: HIV keeps generating new diagnoses and new deaths at a scale that modern medicine has the tools to reduce dramatically. The epidemic hasn't ended. For a country that leads the world in biomedical innovation, that gap between what's possible and what's happening is unacceptable.
text_by_persona.HCI: HIV continues generating new diagnoses and new deaths at a scale that responsible public health management cannot ignore. The epidemic hasn't ended. Assuming it has — and pulling back the systems keeping it in check — is exactly how a controlled problem becomes an uncontrolled one.
text_by_persona.GHI: HIV continues generating new diagnoses and new deaths — here and around the world — at a scale that sustained global public health attention has not yet solved. The epidemic hasn't ended. The institutional commitment required to end it is under pressure at exactly the wrong moment.
